headline: Approved color palette for 72 Concord Street and vinyl window replacement at 18 Manchester Street, both 5-0-0.
summary: The Historic District Commission reviewed two cases. It approved the color palette presented for 72 Concord Street, and approved vinyl replacement windows for 18 Manchester Street on the condition that the applicant provide staff with cost and design details for interior versus exterior muntins.
decisions: Approved the minutes of August 24, 2026 as written.
Approved the color palette as presented for 72 Concord Street, 5-0-0.

Approved the application for 18 Manchester Street to replace windows with vinyl Harvey replacement windows, with the condition that the applicant provide staff with window design and cost for interior and exterior muntins, 5-0-0.

HDC Meeting September 28, 2026                              Page 1 of 4 
 
NASHUA HISTORIC DISTRICT COMMISSION 
 
Monday, September 28, 2026, 6:00 p.m., City Hall, Room 208  
 
HDC Members: 
  
 Robert Vorbach 
 Lisa Law 
 Paige Hultman 
 Alderwoman Patricia Klee 
 Marnie Gordon 
  
 Also present:  
 
 Scott McPhie, Planner 1 
   
MINUTES: 
 
August 24, 2026: 
 
MOTION by Mr. Vorbach to approve the minutes as written 
 
SECONDED by Alderman Klee 
 
MOTION CARRIED UNANIMOUSLY BY VERBAL ROLL CALL OF THE MEMBERS.   
 
Mr. McPhie distributed the memorandum provided to them by Sam Durfee, Planning Director and 
dated August 3, 2026 , saying this memorandum should be us ed to review each of the cases 
presented tonight.    
 
OLD BUSINESS:  
1. Gal Peretz, The Courtland, LLC (Owner) 72 Concord Street (Sheet 65 Lot 91) , 
requesting the following:  replacing all windows with new vinyl windows with 
simulated divided lites, remove and replace siding with wood clapboard siding, 
repair/restore third floor porch, replace all vinyl diamond -pattern lattice with 
square-pattern lattice, repair/replace porch roof and porch ceiling, and install a 
new porch roof finished with architectural asphalt shingles or standing seam 
metal roof.  RB Zone, Ward 3. [FOR THE REVIEW AND APPROVAL OF 
COLORS ONLY] 
Voting on this case: 
 
 Robert Vorbach 
 Lisa Law 
 Paige Hultman 
 Alderwoman Patricia Klee 
     Marnie Gordon
HDC Meeting September 28, 2026                              Page 2 of 4 
 
Mr. Vorbach read the case above and requested the applicant come forward and present it to the 
Commission. 
 
Mr. Peretz expressed concern  why the previous applicant was allowed to use vinyl windows  on 
his Manchester Street property  but he was required to use  original wooden windows for his 
Concord Street property. Mr. Vorbach expressed that the Commission does have an obligation to 
better delineate acceptable materials and a future discussion should be placed on the agenda to sort 
that out. He then requested Mr. McPhie add that to a future agenda.   
 
A discussion ensued concerning the color of a white windows as not representing the current color 
palettes in place at the 72 Concord street property. Alderman Klee said there are no controls over 
color in the HDC, then asked Mr. McPhie to correct her if she was wrong.  Mr. McPhie said the 
criteria provided tonight is what should be relied on to answer that question.  Alderman Klee said 
there is no mention of any restrictions on color.  
 
Alderman Klee said the Commission is looking for applicants to strive to preserve  properties in 
the district in the  best way possible, and vinyl windows are not the best choice  in a historically 
accurate setting.  She also added that the homes on Manchester Street are more working -class 
homes and are very different than the grand homes on Concord Street.  
 
Mr. Peretz cited a home that had vinyl windows on Concord Street. Ms. Law added that home may 
have had those windows before there was an HDC.  Alderman Klee added, or they simply did not 
come before us, and we appreciate that you did and are willing to work with us. 
 
Ms. Law cited a section of the approval criteria that indicated “the general compatibility of exterior 
design and arrangement, texture and materials proposed  to be used in relation to the existing 
building or structure allows the HDC to request a certain type of window or material. A possible 
Fire escape was discussed on the Stark Street side which if the third floor were to be used as living 
space would need to be in place to meet city codes. 
 
Mr. Vorbach expressed  the paint scheme of  beige trim, grayish-blue clapboard, and the current 
reddish-colored door  you presented tonight are totally acceptable  to him . The printer pictures    
show a very dark blue  color to be used on the house , not the current more appropriate color  as 
provided by the samples. Samples are always the best way to determine color. All present agreed 
with that statement. Mr. Peretz said the printer does not represent the actual color  but the sample 
does.  
  
 
Speaking in Favor: 
 
No One 
 
Speaking Against: 
 
No One 
 
END OF THE PUBLIC HEARING: BEGINNING OF THE PUBLIC MEETING 
 
Mr. Vorbach made a motion to approve the color palette as presented. The motion was seconded 
by Alderman Klee.
HDC Meeting September 28, 2026                              Page 3 of 4 
 
The motion passed 5-0-0. 
 
 
 
 
NEW BUSINESS: 
 
1. Medeiros Properties LLC (Owner) Samuel Bacon &  Carol Pelz (Applicants) 18 
Manchester Street (Sheet 67 Lot 89) requesting approval to replace existing 
windows with vinyl Harvey replacement windows, with no changes to the window 
openings.  RC Zone, Ward 3. 
 
Voting on this case: 
 
 Robert Vorbach 
 Lisa Law 
 Paige Hultman 
 Alderwoman Patricia Klee 
 Marnie Gordon   
 
Mr. Vorbach read the case  above and requested the applicant come forward and present  it to the 
Commission. 
 
Mr. Bacon introduced himself and said he was here tonight to request the removal of t he old 
windows at his home due to age and the presence of lead paint and replace them with a Vinyl 
substitute windows. All current windows would be replaced within the same openings  present in 
the home today. The only deviation from the current grid pattern will be to replace one eight-over-
two muntin window with a six-over-two version.   
 
Alderman Klee explained the process to the applicant and said s he, as your Ward Alderman , has 
received compliments from your neighbors on how nice  of a job you have done to clean up the 
home.  
 
Ms. Hultman asked if the windows in place are original  and what type of siding is on the house.   
Mr. Bacon said the windows are likely original, as they are made up of the rope and pulley design. 
 
Ms. Law indicated you could consult with a local lumber company like Currier Lumber in Milford, 
as she did to create replacement interior woodwork in your home. 
 
Mr. Vorbach expressed the more historically authentic window choice would be what is called a 
“simulated divided light” that is p laced on the outside of the glass, whereas your proposal is 
mullion windows with the muntins in the glass that do not look authentic.  
 
Mr. Bacon said he had looked into restoring the windows in kind, but the cost factor was too high. 
He will consult with his builder on what types of windows are available at a fair price point   then 
choosing between either interior or exterior mounted mullions which will be dependent on cost.. 
 
Ms. Hultman asked if the applicant could come back with t he proposed window samples. Mr. 
Bacon was concerned about the cost and the time crunch  involved to do that before the winter .  
Mr. Vorbach appreciated all the efforts the applicant has made, and said we can’t deny vinyl
HDC Meeting September 28, 2026                              Page 4 of 4 
windows but can request the applicant look into the exterior muntin design versus the interior glass 
muntin and send that chosen type to Mr. McPhie for review and comment.     
 
Speaking in Favor: 
 
No One 
 
Speaking Against: 
 
No One 
 
 
Mr. Vorbach made a motion to approve the application with  the condition that the applicant 
provide staff with the window design and cost for the interior muntins and the cost for the window 
with the exterior muntins for review and comment , letting staff know what the final choice will 
be. Alderman Klee seconded the motion.   
 
The motion passed 5-0-0. 
 
 
Mr. Vorbach thanked the applicant and said to feel free to call him concerning the application of 
the screening materials. 
 
 
The communication section of the meeting ensued, and another request was made to clarify the 
approval criteria.  Alderman Klee volunteered to work on the aldermanic side to bring those 
clarifications forward. Mr. McPhie took the time to address any general questions related to 
Historic District Commissions in general.   The Concord, Manchester and Portsmouth HDC 
regulations were suggested as a possible comparison point to start with. 
 
ADJOURN  
 
MOTION by Mr. Vorbach made a motion to adjourn at 7:10 PM 
 
MOTION CARRIED Unanimously  
 
 
END OF THE PUBLIC HEARING: BEGINNING OF THE PUBLIC MEETING
